newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters in pivotal role - Bolger's press sec.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters in pivotal role - Bolger's press sec.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger's chief press secretary, Richard Griffin, said on Saturday that New Zealand First leader Winston Peters would be pivotal in the make-up of the government after the general election.
However, Griffin said, Peters' support would come at a price.

Peters has refused to rule out the possibility of a coalition with the ruling conservative National party after the election, New Zealand's first under a proportional voting system that favours minority or coalition governments.
His attacks on the Labour party have been far less regular and less vitriolic than those on Bolger and the National party.
"Where Peters goes, I guess, goes government," Griffin said in an interview on TV3.
Political columnist and cartoonist Tom Scott, on a panel putting questions to Griffin, asked if Griffin was hinting that Peters could support National.
"I think the ask would be so big he would probably split the National party in half," Griffin said, adding that Peters could well do the same to Labour.

Polling booths closed at 7.00 p.m., with the first results expected shortly after 8.00 p.m. Final results, not including special votes which must be counted within 10 days, should be published around 10.30 or 11.00 p.m.
